A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DuoGPT work and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–C. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original DuoGPT experiments, including language-model performance, GPU speedups, calibration sensitivity, and algorithm latency.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix C, including benchmark results, sensitivity studies, and GPU measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same activation-aware pruning, dense-output residual correction, pruning scores, weight updates, and efficient implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions retain C4 calibration, WikiText2 perplexity, the same seven zero-shot benchmarks, and five-shot GSM8K evaluation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain identical baseline membership: SparseGPT and Wanda variants, ShortGPT, 2SSP, BlockPruner, SliceGPT, R-Sparse, and TEAL appear in the same experiments.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B–C retain the same model configurations, calibration sample counts and sequence lengths, sparsity settings, metrics, and speedup measurement procedures.

E4.justification: The sparsity sweeps, threshold-based activation compatibility study, SRAM-loading analysis, calibration-size and sequence-length sensitivity studies, and algorithm-efficiency analysis are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither introduces repeated-seed results, confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and Figures 3–6 retain the same numerical results and trends. For example, Table 2 reports DuoGPT average accuracy of 60.52%, WikiText2 perplexity of 8.58, and speedup of 1.39× in both versions.

T1.justification: The definitions and derivations in Sections 3–4 and the proofs in Appendix A are unchanged, including the calibration solution and Cholesky-based identities.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and accuracy, efficiency, and scalability claims. The added code-availability sentence does not revise those claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of residual compensation, sparsity-dependent performance, and calibration sensitivity remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the limitation that a full GPU spMspV kernel implementation is future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds 'Code is available at Github' to the abstract, with a direct hyperlink to the DuoGPT repository; v1 provides no such pointer. Implementation details and experimental settings elsewhere are unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or functionality.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, and the reference list are unchanged. The positioning relative to activation sparsity, one-shot pruning, and OBC remains the same.

P1.justification: v2 adds one code-availability sentence and replaces 'Preprint. Under review.' with the NeurIPS 2025 conference notice, alongside the updated arXiv stamp. The remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract sentence produces limited first-page reflow, and the publication footer changes. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–6 retain their designs, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: The new direct implementation link modestly improves code discoverability and reproducibility documentation compared with v1. The scientific evidence, proofs, and limitations are unchanged. This limited benefit concerns the access information supplied by the paper; the PDFs alone do not establish the linked code's completeness or functionality.
